content.tldr: Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) mandates that users substantiate identity by presenting credentials across at least two distinct authentication categories.
content.simple_explanation: Authentication factors are categorized into three core classes: Knowledge (something you know, like a password or PIN), Possession (something you have, like a hardware FIDO2 key, authenticator app TOTP, or smartcard), and Inherence (something you are, like a fingerprint or facial scan). True multi-factor authentication requires combining elements from different categories; demanding two separate passwords constitutes two-step verification, not two-factor.
content.real_world_example: Withdrawing cash from an ATM: you must present your physical bank card (Possession) and enter your private 4-digit PIN (Knowledge); without both distinct factors, the terminal denies the withdrawal.
content.why_it_matters_and_pitfalls: SMS-based OTP verification is vulnerable to SIM swapping, SS7 signaling redirection, and real-time reverse-proxy phishing (Evilginx). High-assurance architectures require FIDO2/WebAuthn hardware tokens, which cryptographically bind the authentication assertion to the origin domain.
